title: Filler-Token Faithfulness: Do Models Need Their Stated Reasoning at All?

original_idea.body: Filler-Token Faithfulness. Problem: the Lanham filler/'...' replacement variant is rarely tested on modern small reasoning models. Direction: run the Lanham intervention suite (early answering, truncation, adding mistakes, filler replacement) on a small open reasoning model, measure how much accuracy depends on CoT content, characterize which task types show CoT-as-rationalization.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: mapping where CoT is decorative tells where monitoring is trustworthy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inherited Lanham intervention suite on a small reasoning model.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused per-task reliance characterization; multiple interventions add scope.

novelty.reasoning: Lanham's suite is published; re-running on modern small models is incremental (overlaps gen-3457).

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The Lanham intervention suite is established; this is largely a replication on newer models.
